sections.st: What is Clamshell Packaging? — Formats, Sealing and Applications
leads: Clamshell packaging is a two-part thermoformed plastic packaging format — a hinged cavity structure that folds closed to enclose and display the product on both sides. Unlike blister packaging (product in cavity sealed against flat foil or film), a clamshell unit is fully formed plastic on both faces — giving 360-degree clear plastic visibility and structural protection without a separate backing material.

sections.st: 3 Sealing Methods — Heat Seal, RF/Ultrasonic and Snap-Close
leads: The sealing method determines tamper evidence, opening force, consumer accessibility, and equipment requirement. Choosing the wrong method creates either under-secured packaging or consumer-hostile packaging:

rows: Interlocking thermoformed tabs — no separate sealing operation. Consumer snaps open and closed.
Standard retail where tamper-evidence not required
Heat and pressure at 140–180°C on the full sealing flange. Irreversible permanent bond. Seal breakage visible.
Pharma OTC, consumer healthcare, premium retail tamper-evident
RF electromagnetic energy or high-freq. vibration creates molecular-level weld. Stronger than heat sealing. Permanent.
Maximum — cannot be separated without destruction

faqs.q: What is clamshell blister packaging and how does it differ from standard blister?
faqs.a: Clamshell blister packaging combines a deep thermoformed clamshell cavity with a flat backing card or blister base. The product is enclosed in the clear clamshell cavity; the backing card carries branding, barcode, and retail display information. Unlike standard blister packaging (cavity sealed directly with foil or Tyvek), clamshell blister packaging uses a formed plastic front with a flat card or plastic back — giving both product visibility and retail display functionality. Euro-hole standard for pegboard display.

faqs.q: What is the difference between heat-sealed and snap-close clamshell packaging?
faqs.a: Snap-close clamshell uses interlocking thermoformed tabs — no heat or equipment required, consumer-resealable, not tamper-evident. Heat-sealed clamshell uses heat and pressure (140–180°C) to create a permanent perimeter seal — irreversible, tamper-evident, requires a heat sealing machine on the packaging line. Snap-close for standard retail. Heat-sealed where tamper evidence is required (pharmaceutical OTC, consumer healthcare).

faqs.q: What materials are clamshell packaging produced from?
faqs.a: PVC (standard, most cost-efficient), PETG (high clarity, premium surface finish, good impact resistance), APET (maximum optical clarity, food-contact grade available), and recycled rPET (30–100% PCR content for sustainability and EPR compliance). PVC for standard retail. PETG and APET for premium clear clamshell packaging where product presentation is priority.
